---
title: "Markov models ([markov_model])"
---

A `[markov_model]` block declares a Markov-chain endpoint: the observed variable is a
discrete *state*, and the model describes how it moves between states. Two families are
available:

- **`type = ctmm`** (the default) — a **continuous-time Markov model**: the
  dynamics are the transition intensities between states. ferx builds the generator
  matrix `Q`, forms the transition-probability matrix `P(Δt) = expm(Q·Δt)`, and scores
  each consecutive pair of state observations — see
  [Continuous-time Markov models](../estimation/ctmm.qmd) for the estimation side.
- **`type = dtmm`** — a **discrete-time Markov model**: each `transition` is the
  *probability* of moving between states from one record to the next, the NONMEM
  `PREVIOUS`-DV `$PRED` model. See
  [Discrete-time Markov models](#discrete-time-markov-models-type-dtmm) below and
  [the estimation page](../estimation/dtmm.qmd).

::: {.callout-note}
The `[markov_model]` endpoint requires the `markov` cargo feature
(`cargo build --features markov`). It is opt-in while maturing; see the plan.
:::

## The transition-list form (recommended)

Declare the states — each bound to its integer **DV code** — and one line per allowed
transition with its intensity:

```default
[parameters]
  theta LQ01(-0.7, -6.0, 3.0)   # log intensity awake -> asleep
  theta LQ10(-1.2, -6.0, 3.0)   # log intensity asleep -> awake

[markov_model]
  type   = ctmm                     # ctmm (only value for now)
  cmt    = 5                        # data-file CMT for the state observations
  states = [awake=0, asleep=1]      # label = DV integer code (explicit, never positional)
  transition awake  -> asleep = exp(LQ01)   # intensity q_{awake→asleep} ≥ 0
  transition asleep -> awake  = exp(LQ10)
```

- **`states`** — a bracketed list of `label=code` entries. `code` is the integer value
  that appears in the `DV` column for that state; `label` names the state for the
  `transition` lines. States may be coded with any non-negative integers (e.g. `1`/`2`),
  not only `0…S−1`. Codes must be unique.
- **`transition A -> B = <expr>`** — one per allowed transition. `<expr>` is the
  intensity `q_{A→B} ≥ 0`, written as any θ/η/covariate/`[individual_parameters]`
  expression (wrap it in `exp(...)` to keep it positive, as above). The generator's
  diagonal `q_jj = −Σ_{k≠j} q_jk` is filled automatically — **you never write it**.
- **`cmt`** — the CMT column value carrying the state observations. Rows on this CMT are
  read as integer states; the same CMT cannot also be a Gaussian (`[error_model]`)
  endpoint.
- **`type`** — optional; **defaults to `ctmm`**. Omitting the line parses as a CTMM.
  `dtmm` selects the [discrete-time model](#discrete-time-markov-models-type-dtmm);
  `mctmm` is recognized but rejected as "not yet supported".

### Bare numeric states

Labels are optional. A purely numeric model reads:

```default
[markov_model]
  type   = ctmm
  cmt    = 5
  states = [0, 1]
  transition 0 -> 1 = exp(LQ01)
  transition 1 -> 0 = exp(LQ10)
```

## Data format

The `DV` column holds the **integer state code** for each observation — the same numeric
convention as every other ferx endpoint (no string labels). Rows are ordinary
observations (`EVID = 0`, `MDV = 0`); a missing `DV` is skipped as `MDV = 1`. The
likelihood conditions on each subject's first observed state, so no `EVID = 3` /
occupancy-flag rows are needed (unlike the NONMEM CTMM dataset convention).

```default
ID,TIME,DV,CMT,EVID,MDV
1,0.0,0,5,0,0
1,1.1,0,5,0,0
1,1.8,1,5,0,0
1,4.6,0,5,0,0
```

An observed `DV` that is not one of the declared `states` codes is rejected fail-loud at
fit setup (naming the CMT and the offending value). Each subject's CTMM rows must be
**non-decreasing in `TIME`** — the reader does not reorder observations, so an out-of-order
subject is rejected at fit setup rather than silently dropped.

## Random effects and covariates

An intensity may carry between-subject variability and covariates:

```default
[parameters]
  theta LQ01(-0.7, -6.0, 3.0)
  theta LQ10(-1.2, -6.0, 3.0)
  theta BAGE(0.0, -3.0, 3.0)
  omega ETA_Q ~ 0.1

[covariates]
  AGE continuous

[markov_model]
  type   = ctmm
  cmt    = 5
  states = [awake=0, asleep=1]
  transition awake  -> asleep = exp(LQ01 + BAGE * AGE + ETA_Q)
  transition asleep -> awake  = exp(LQ10)
```

The generator is built once per subject from a **baseline** covariate snapshot (a
*time-homogeneous* generator). A covariate that is time-varying in the data is therefore
rejected at fit setup rather than silently frozen. For the same reason a bare `TIME` in an
intensity is rejected at parse (it would silently resolve to 0). Intensities are evaluated
with per-subject (BSV) η only, so an inter-occasion (`[iov]` / κ) reference is rejected.

An intensity is a **rate** and must evaluate non-negative for every subject: a
parameter/covariate regime that drives an off-diagonal negative makes the generator
non-stochastic, and that subject's contribution is treated as degenerate (it repels the
optimizer) rather than silently scored. Write intensities on a scale that stays positive
— e.g. `exp(...)` — rather than an unconstrained linear form.

## Drug- / PD-driven intensities (time-inhomogeneous `Q(t)`)

An intensity may instead depend on the **model state** — a drug concentration or a
pharmacodynamic response that evolves over time — making the generator *time-inhomogeneous*,
`Q(t) = f(state(t))`. Reference an ODE state by name in the transition (there is no `Cc`
builtin — write a concentration as `central / V`, exactly as a drug-driven survival hazard
does):

```default
[structural_model]
  ode(obs_cmt=central, states=[depot, central])

[odes]
  d/dt(depot)   = -KA * depot
  d/dt(central) =  KA * depot - (CL/V) * central

[markov_model]
  type   = ctmm
  cmt    = 5
  states = [awake=0, asleep=1]
  transition awake  -> asleep = exp(LQ01 + SLOPE * (central / V))
  transition asleep -> awake  = exp(LQ10)
```

When an intensity references a state, ferx solves the model's ODE system for the subject and
integrates the occupancy equation `dP/dτ = P·Q(state(t))` (forward Kolmogorov, so
`P(Δt)[from,to] = Pr(to | from)`) over each observation gap (there is
no closed form once `Q` varies within the gap), scoring the same
`−Σ log P(Δt_m)[s_m, s_{m+1}]`. Any transform is written inline (e.g. an Emax effect
`EMAX * R / (EC50 + R)` on a response state `R`); a state reached only through an
`[individual_parameters]` value is rejected — reference the state **directly** in the
`transition` line. This requires an ODE (`[odes]`) model; the occupancy integration uses the
model's ODE tolerance (`TOL`).

The `[odes]` solve behind a drug-driven intensity runs under the individual parameters
evaluated once, at `TIME = 0` (dose quantities — `F`, `ALAG`, `D{n}`, absorption — are read
at each dose record). So an `[individual_parameters]` value that reads `TIME` and reaches a
state the intensities read — through the `[odes]` right-hand side or an `init(...)` seed —
would be frozen there while the Gaussian predictions read it at every record. `fit()`,
`ferx check`, `run_covariance()` and `run_sir()` refuse such a model with `E_ENDPOINT_TIME_DEPENDENT_PK`, naming the parameter
([#1918](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1918)); a `TIME`-dependent parameter
the intensities' states do not depend on, and a time-homogeneous CTMM, are unaffected.

The same solve reads the **baseline** covariate snapshot, so a covariate that is
time-varying in the data and reaches such a parameter — `CL = TVCL * (WT / 70)`, with `WT`
changing within a subject — is refused the same way, with `E_ENDPOINT_TV_COVARIATE` on
`[markov_model]`, naming the covariate and the parameter
([#1854](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1854)), although no intensity names
the covariate. A time-varying covariate on a dose quantity (`KA`, `F`, …) or on a parameter
the intensities' states do not depend on is accepted. A change counts wherever it is
recorded, including on the `[markov_model]` state rows themselves — a subject whose first
row is a state row at `WT = 1`, with every dose at `WT = 0`, has a baseline of `WT = 1`
and is refused too. So does a row the reader drops: the baseline is the first value on
any row, so a leading `WT = 1` row skipped for a missing `DV` (or removed by
`[data_selection]`) still sets it, and a subject whose every kept row has `WT = 0` is
refused.

A complete runnable model is `examples/ctmm_pd_2state.ferx` (with `data/ctmm_pd_2state.csv`):
a concentration-driven 2-state process where ferx recovers the transition intensities and the
drug effect from the Gillespie-simulated data.

## Discrete-time Markov models (`type = dtmm`)

A DTMM uses the same `states` / `transition` grammar, but the right-hand side of each
`transition` is a **transition probability**, not an intensity: the probability that the
state observed at a record is `B`, given that the state observed at the subject's previous
record was `A`. There is no generator and no `expm`:

```default
[parameters]
  theta A_AS(-0.5, -10.0, 10.0)
  theta B_DOSE(0.2, -10.0, 10.0)
  theta A_SA(-0.5, -10.0, 10.0)
  omega ETA_AS ~ 0.3
  omega ETA_SA ~ 0.3

[markov_model]
  type   = dtmm
  cmt    = 5
  states = [awake=0, asleep=1]
  transition awake  -> asleep = inv_logit(A_AS + B_DOSE * DOSE + ETA_AS)
  transition asleep -> awake  = inv_logit(A_SA + ETA_SA)
```

- The **stay probability** `P_jj = 1 − Σ_{k≠j} P_jk` is filled in automatically — you
  never write it.
- Each probability must lie in `[0, 1]` and a row's off-diagonals must sum to at most `1`.
  A parameter value that breaks this for the row being stepped from is **penalized**: the
  subject repels the optimizer, rather than scoring a probability outside `[0, 1]`. Writing
  each probability through `inv_logit(...)` (alias `expit`) keeps it in range; with more
  than one transition out of a state, use the cumulative-logit form below so the row sum
  stays below 1 too.
- A change of state the data contain that no `transition` line declares has probability 0
  for every parameter value. It is refused at fit setup (`E_CTMM_RECORDS`), naming the CMT,
  the two states and the `TIME` of the step.

### What is scored

For each subject, the `DV` codes of its rows on `cmt`, in record order, form a chain
`s_0, s_1, …`, and the data term is

```default
−Σ_{k ≥ 1} log P_k[s_{k−1}, s_k]
```

- **The first record is conditioned on** — it contributes nothing, as in a
  `PREVIOUS`-DV `$PRED` where the first record of an individual has no previous value.
  There is no `init` / stationary distribution.
- **A step is a record, not a time unit.** `P_k` does not depend on the spacing of the
  records; irregular intervals are accepted and each step uses the same per-record
  probability. To make a probability depend on time, reference `TIME`.
- **The probabilities are those of the current record.** `P_k` is evaluated at record
  `k`, so a `TIME` term reads the time of the record being scored, not the previous one.
- **A missing state links to the last observed one.** A row with a missing `DV` (or
  `MDV = 1`) is not part of the chain; the next observed record steps from the last
  observed state, which is what a `PREVIOUS`-DV `$PRED` reading the last observed `DV`
  does.

### More than two ordered states: cumulative logit

For `K > 2` ordered states, write the probabilities of each previous state `j` as
differences of a cumulative logit, `P(s ≤ k | prev = j) = inv_logit(α_k − γ_j)`, with
monotone cut-points `α_k = α_{k−1} + exp(δ_k)` so every row is a valid distribution. The
stay probability is the diagonal ferx fills in:

```default
[parameters]
  theta A1(0.0, -10.0, 10.0)
  theta D2(0.0, -10.0, 10.0)    # α_2 = α_1 + exp(D2)
  theta G1(1.0, -10.0, 10.0)    # shift when the previous state was mild
  theta G2(2.0, -10.0, 10.0)    # … severe
  omega ETA ~ 0.3

[markov_model]
  type   = dtmm
  cmt    = 5
  states = [none=0, mild=1, severe=2]
  transition none   -> mild   = inv_logit(A1 + exp(D2) + ETA) - inv_logit(A1 + ETA)
  transition none   -> severe = 1 - inv_logit(A1 + exp(D2) + ETA)
  transition mild   -> none   = inv_logit(A1 - G1 + ETA)
  transition mild   -> severe = 1 - inv_logit(A1 + exp(D2) - G1 + ETA)
  transition severe -> none   = inv_logit(A1 - G2 + ETA)
  transition severe -> mild   = inv_logit(A1 + exp(D2) - G2 + ETA) - inv_logit(A1 - G2 + ETA)
```

### Covariates, `TIME` and drug effects

A transition probability may reference θ, η, `[individual_parameters]` values, covariates
and `TIME`. Covariates are read at the subject's **baseline** snapshot, so a covariate that
is time-varying in the data is refused at fit setup (`E_ENDPOINT_TV_COVARIATE`) rather than
silently frozen; per-record covariates are planned. A reference to an ODE model state (a
drug-driven transition probability) is rejected at parse — use a `type = ctmm` endpoint for
a drug-driven transition model for now. As for the CTMM, IOV (κ) is not supported.

## Current limitations

- `type = mctmm` (minimal-CTMM) — planned.
- DTMM: time-varying covariates and drug-driven (model-state) transition probabilities,
  and simulation / prediction — planned.
- The matrix (`q12 = …`) spelling and an `init` occupancy vector — planned.
- Simulation / prediction of a CTMM endpoint — planned (`simulate()` refuses both
  families with `E_CTMM_UNSUPPORTED`).
- A drug/PD-driven intensity requires an ODE model and a state referenced **directly** in the
  transition; analytic (closed-form) PK as a driver is planned.
- Estimators: `focei` (default), `saem`, and `imp`. Gauss–Newton (`gn`/`gn_hybrid`) is
  rejected (its gradient is Gaussian-specific).
